ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.76 to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) for the unexcused off-route segment; no account flag required.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a route-deviation complaint on a completed RydeTAXI trip, so the fare model is metered: distance driven enters the fare directly, and the remedy is RD-2's per-km refund for any segment not exempted by RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 [F1][F6][RD-2].

RD-1: the trace records one off-route segment, F3 — 18:46–18:52, 3.50 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.54 km, up to 752 m off the optimal route, adding 1.96 km. That segment must be reviewed under RD-3, RD-4 and RD-5 [F3][RD-1].

RD-4: the driver's statement claims a breakdown and points to the LTA feed [F8]. There is a genuine vehicle-breakdown incident on the optimal route, reported 18:27 at 0 m from it [F11], but the timing does not support an exemption for this segment: the detour ran 18:46–18:52, and the incident report at 18:27 is the record the driver relied on; the speed-band facts [F9][F10] cover 18:19–19:15 but they sit on the optimal corridor generally and speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) is nowhere near the band 1–2 congestion RD-4(b) contemplates, so the code's ✗ on RD-4(a) stands and no traffic fact exempts this stretch [F9][F10][F11][RD-4].

RD-5 / RD-3: there is no in-app chat at all between rider and driver [F7], and the driver's account of the trip is a post-trip written statement, not a rider message [F8]; a driver's claim that the rider agreed is not consent (G11), and nothing in the record shows a rider-named stop or a rider message before 18:46:55. The segment therefore has no consent ground: it counts under RD-5 [F7][F8][RD-5][RD-3].

Amount: the per-km rate is this trip's distance fare over distance km, $33.33 ÷ 23.64 km = $1.40992/km (the record's own trace states $1.4099/km) [F4][F6][RD-2]. The one counted segment adds 3.50 − 1.54 = 1.96 km, so 1.96 km × $1.40992/km = $2.7635, rounded to $2.76 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The fare record's own excess-distance line ($3.06 for 2.17 km) includes unmatched rolling distance outside any segment, which RD-2 leaves unrefunded, so the refund is the segment figure, not $3.06 [F4][RD-2].

RD-6: the driver's profile shows 2 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld, and the trace's RD-6 check is ✗ (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so the breach is not "repeated" and no account flag attaches [F14][RD-6]. The rider's profile is not used to decide anything [F13][RD-6].

Evidence: the record settles every element — an off-route segment [F3], a metered fare with distance fare and distance km [F4][F6], no chat [F7] and a post-trip statement [F8] — so the ruling can be computed without gaps [RD-2][RD-5].

Safety: I read the complaint, the driver's statement and the (empty) chat [F7][F8]. The complaint is a fare/route objection, the statement is a route justification; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so the screen is none [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

segment_findings.reason: No rider message exists before the segment start (18:46:55) — the in-app chat is empty [F7] — and the only account of an agreement is the driver's post-trip statement, which is a claim, not rider consent (G11). No rider-named stop and no route the rider agreed to; the 1.96 km extra on this stretch is unexcused and refundable under RD-2 [F3][F7][F8][RD-5][RD-2].
